concepts.name: Origins and Historical Evolution of Hindustani Music
key_dimensions: Divergence from Carnatic music post-13th century under Sultanate influence
Role of Amir Khusrau in synthesizing Persian and Indian elements
Transition from Vedic Sama Veda traditions to medieval court music
Influence of Bhakti and Sufi movements on thematic content and ragas

concepts.name: Raga: Structure, Classification, and Rules
key_dimensions: Distinction between Arohana (ascent) and Avarohana (descent) and their asymmetry in ragas
Vadi (most important note) and Samvadi (second most important) — significance and interval rule
Pakad (characteristic phrase) as raga identity vs. mere scale definition
Classification by Thaat system vs. older Mela system — key differences and UPSC traps

concepts.name: Thaat System of Raga Classification (Bhatkhande's Framework)
key_dimensions: V.N. Bhatkhande's 10 parent Thaats and their derivation logic
Thaat as a scale vs. Raga as a performable entity — critical distinction
Mapping of prominent ragas to their parent Thaats (e.g., Bhairavi, Yaman, Bhairav)
Comparison with Carnatic Melakarta system — number, structure, and philosophical differences

concepts.name: Time Theory of Ragas (Raga-Time Association)
key_dimensions: Concept of Prahar (3-hour divisions) and raga association with specific prahars
Seasonal ragas — Megh, Malhar, Basant — and their contextual performance rules
Physiological and emotional basis of time theory as argued in classical texts
UPSC trap: Ragas that are exceptions or performed at multiple times (e.g., Bhairavi as a concluding raga)

concepts.name: Tala System in Hindustani Music
key_dimensions: Structure of Tala: Vibhag, Matra, Sam, Khali — definitions and functional roles
Key Talas: Teentaal (16 beats), Ektaal (12), Jhaptaal (10), Rupaktaal (7) — beat compositions
Concept of Laya (tempo): Vilambit, Madhya, Drut — and their use across genres
Difference between Hindustani Tala system and Carnatic Tala system (Suladi Sapta Talas)

concepts.name: Gharana System: Origin, Purpose, and Transmission
key_dimensions: Definition of Gharana and its sociological basis — hereditary vs. discipleship models
Guru-Shishya Parampara as the vehicle of gharana knowledge transmission
Geographic anchoring of gharanas and their patronage by princely states
Decline of traditional gharana boundaries in the post-independence concert music era

concepts.name: Khayal Gayaki and Its Major Gharanas
key_dimensions: Khayal's origin — attributed to Amir Khusrau or Sultan Hussain Sharqi (Jaunpur) — contested history
Gwalior Gharana as the oldest Khayal gharana — features: clarity, simplicity, Shuddha swar
Agra Gharana — emphasis on Nom-Tom Alaap, Dhrupad influence, powerful voice
Jaipur-Atrauli Gharana (Alladiya Khan) — complex taans, rare ragas, Tayyari; Kirana Gharana — sur-centric, Bhava, slow elaboration (Abdul Karim Khan)

concepts.name: Dhrupad: The Oldest Surviving Classical Form
key_dimensions: Four Vanis (styles) of Dhrupad: Gauhar, Dagur, Khandar, Nauhar — distinct characteristics
Structural format: Alaap (Nom-Tom) → Bandish in four parts (Sthayi, Antara, Sanchari, Abhog)
Dagar Gharana as the primary surviving Dhrupad tradition — key exponents
Dhrupad vs. Khayal: ornamentation philosophy, tempo approach, lyrical content differences

concepts.name: Thumri, Dadra, and Semi-Classical Forms
key_dimensions: Thumri as 'light classical' — Shringar rasa dominance, Raga flexibility (Raga ki pakad loosened)
Two styles of Thumri: Purbi (Banaras) ang vs. Punjabi (patiala) ang
Dadra vs. Thumri — tala difference (Dadra tala: 6 beats) and lighter emotional tenor
Other semi-classical forms: Chaiti, Kajri, Hori, Tappa — their regional and seasonal contexts

concepts.name: Kirana Gharana and Sur-Centric Aesthetic
key_dimensions: Founded by Abdul Karim Khan and Abdul Wahid Khan — geographic origin in Kirana (Uttar Pradesh)
Signature style: slow, meditative Vilambit Khayal, emphasis on Gamak and Meend
Notable descendants: Hirabai Barodekar, Roshanara Begum, Gangubai Hangal, Bhimsen Joshi
Bhimsen Joshi's synthesis of Kirana and other styles — UPSC relevance as Bharat Ratna recipient

concepts.name: Patiala Gharana and Taan-Centric Tradition
key_dimensions: Founded by Fateh Ali Khan and Ali Baksh — Punjab court patronage
Signature style: elaborate, fast taans, gamak taans, and rich ornamentation
Synthesis of Dhrupad, Khayal, and Thumri elements within the gharana
Notable exponents: Bade Ghulam Ali Khan — crossover appeal and film music contribution

concepts.name: Sarod and Its Gharanas
key_dimensions: Sarod's origin: descended from Afghan Rabab — not a direct Sitar relative (common confusion)
Senia-Bangash Gharana (Gwalior) vs. Shahjahanpur Gharana — stylistic differences
Ali Akbar Khan and Amjad Ali Khan as primary 20th-century exponents
Sarod's structural features: fretless fingerboard, metal strings, resonating gourd — comparison with Sitar

concepts.name: Sitar and the Imdadkhani (Etawah) Gharana
key_dimensions: Sitar's origin: attributed to Amir Khusrau — contested; structural evolution from Veena family
Imdadkhani Gharana founded by Imdad Khan — Gayaki ang (singing style) on Sitar
Ravi Shankar (Maihar Gharana) vs. Vilayat Khan (Imdadkhani) — two dominant 20th-century styles
Ravi Shankar's global role: collaboration with Yehudi Menuhin, George Harrison — cultural diplomacy angle

concepts.name: Tabla and Its Gharanas
key_dimensions: Six major Tabla gharanas: Delhi, Ajrada, Lucknow, Farukhabad, Banaras, Punjab — distinct bols and styles
Delhi Gharana (oldest) — crisp, syllabic bols; Lucknow Gharana — lyrical, Kathak-linked style
Banaras Gharana — heavy, resonant strokes; Punjab Gharana — influence of folk Dhol tradition
Tabla vs. Pakhawaj — historical relationship and role differentiation in Khayal vs. Dhrupad

concepts.name: Bansuri (Flute) Tradition: Pannalal Ghosh and Hariprasad Chaurasia
key_dimensions: Pannalal Ghosh's role in elevating Bansuri from folk to classical concert instrument
Hariprasad Chaurasia's Maihar Gharana training and innovation in raga elaboration on flute
Bansuri's absence of frets — implication for microtonal (Shruti) expression
Bansuri in iconography (Krishna) vs. its late classical concert music adoption — contrast

concepts.name: Shehnai Tradition and Bismillah Khan
key_dimensions: Shehnai's ceremonial (Mangal vadya) origins vs. Bismillah Khan's elevation to concert platform
Bismillah Khan's Banaras Gharana background and synthesis of folk/classical elements
Shehnai's performance at India's first Independence Day — historical and symbolic significance
Bismillah Khan as Bharat Ratna recipient — UPSC factual anchor with cultural diplomacy context

concepts.name: Vocal Ornamentation Techniques (Alankaras) in Hindustani Music
key_dimensions: Key ornaments: Meend (glide), Gamak (oscillation), Murki (quick turn), Kan swar (grace note)
Andolan (slow oscillation on specific notes) — raga-specific application vs. general use
Distinction between Hindustani and Carnatic ornamentation (Gamakas) — philosophy of continuity vs. discreteness
UPSC trap: Confusing Taan (fast melodic run) with Tana/Alankara — functional distinctions

concepts.name: Alaap, Jod, Jhala: Instrumental Raga Elaboration Structure
key_dimensions: Alaap: Free-rhythm, unaccompanied raga exposition — role in establishing raga identity
Jod: Introduction of rhythmic pulse (without Tala) — transitional phase
Jhala: Fast rhythmic section using side drone strings — climax before bandish
Comparison with vocal Khayal structure (Vilambit → Drut) — parallelism and differences

concepts.name: Maihar Gharana and Allauddin Khan's Legacy
key_dimensions: Allauddin Khan as multi-instrumentalist founder — unique 'school' rather than single-instrument gharana
Disciples: Ravi Shankar (Sitar), Ali Akbar Khan (Sarod), Pannalal Ghosh (Bansuri), Nikhil Banerjee
Maihar Gharana's synthetic approach — integration of Dhrupad discipline with Khayal expressiveness
Annapurna Devi (Allauddin Khan's daughter) — deliberate withdrawal from public performance as cultural narrative

concepts.name: Institutional Framework for Hindustani Music: Bodies and Awards
key_dimensions: Sangeet Natak Akademi — statutory body under Ministry of Culture, awards and fellowship structure
Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship (Ratna Sadasya) vs. Sangeet Natak Akademi Award — distinction
All India Radio (Akashvani) Audition System — role in standardizing and democratizing classical music
SPIC MACAY, ITC-SRA — non-governmental promotion bodies; Bharat Ratna recipients in music (factual traps)
